headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Continue’s filesystem/MCP access can feed Replit Agent’s writable, secret-bearing workspace and action-taking loop.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while Replit Agent can read/write the same class of workspace files in a persistent Repl filesystem. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent consumes the other’s file output. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Continue reads Replit-authored files as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF both agents operate on the same workspace path, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable shared workspace access between the two agents.
Require manual review of any file one agent writes before the other reads it.
Use separate repos or directories per agent.
Add provenance tags to agent-generated files.
requires-engineering: enforce content filtering on files passed between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and has broad network egress; Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration and can egress broadly. If they share a workspace, sensitive material from Replit can be exposed through Continue’s outputs or upstream model calls. The blast radius includes secrets and code, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF the two agents share any workspace containing secrets or deployment config, leakage risk exists.
IF Continue forwards file contents to its model provider, sensitive Replit data can leave the workspace.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared directory.
Use separate workspaces for code and secrets.
Turn off or restrict network access for the agent handling sensitive files.
Redact secrets before either agent processes files.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on agent file reads and outbound prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have write_filesystem and broad network egress; Replit Agent also has execute_shell, install_packages, spawn_subprocesses, and modify_git_state. In a shared workspace, concurrent edits and git mutations can collide, and Continue’s filesystem-based shared state makes overlap plausible. Because the conflict can corrupt code or repo state irreversibly, high fits.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same files or branch, race conditions can corrupt state.
IF Replit Agent modifies git while Continue edits the same workspace, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch or directory.
Serialize write access with a simple operator checklist.
Pause one agent while the other is making changes.
Review git diffs before merging either agent’s output.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspace writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can produce code changes or file edits that Replit Agent may then act on inside a shell-capable environment. Replit Agent’s toolset lets it install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses, so unverified upstream output can cascade into concrete actions. That default action-taking path makes high appropriate.
conditions: IF Replit Agent consumes Continue-generated code or instructions without verification, errors can propagate into shell actions.
IF Continue writes a mistaken patch that Replit Agent applies, downstream damage can spread.
mitigations: Require human approval before Replit Agent executes any Continue-produced change.
Compare proposed edits against tests before applying them.
Use a staging branch for all cross-agent handoffs.
Ask Continue to emit explicit assumptions and uncertainties.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Continue is open-source and docs-only, while Replit Agent is closed-source and handles secrets plus deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. If regulated data such as secrets or sensitive code is placed in the shared Replit workspace, the pair can create retention and residency ambiguity. The profiles do not prove a specific legal breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the Replit workspace, compliance review is required.
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the IDE extension and Replit cloud workspace, mismatch risk exists.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Document retention and deletion handling for both tools.
Use synthetic or masked data for development.
Review vendor terms before placing sensitive data in Replit.
requires-engineering: formalize a data-processing agreement and residency controls.
